findings.summary: The audited commit does not preserve symbol clusters across the requested five-family held-out matrix.
findings.evidence: All five fresh valid cases fail under /tmp/rustuml-diff-one-17888365 --no-oracle. The failure mode is consistent: one side of the explicit/fallback pair is flattened or loses its intermediate cluster owner, so the container-level header model never runs for that cluster. The broken cases cover node fallback at root, database fallback nested in a frame, explicit frame nested in a cloud, explicit rectangle at root, and cloud fallback at root.

findings.summary: The narrow header-stack patch is real but insufficient for acceptance.
findings.evidence: Surviving symbol clusters do show the intended stereotype/title ordering: explicit node, explicit database, root fallback frame, nested fallback rectangle, and nested explicit cloud each render visible stereotype lines in the expected position. The strict failures therefore reject the broader mechanism claim on model completeness, not because the checker found a fixture-shaped overfit in the changed lines.

findings.summary: No fixture-shaped logic, unexplained output surgery, or comparator manipulation was found in the audited implementation diff.
findings.evidence: The changed Rust paths contain only named Java-cited constants, text-stack helpers, and call-site rewiring. Searches over the audited files found no held-out filenames, mechanism-name strings, test-diagram reads, include_str/include_bytes additions, or coordinate-keyed SVG rewriting. The rejection is about failing held-outs, not about dishonest implementation tactics.
